name: Hagar
bio:
Hagar is Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abram as a wife because of Sarah's barrenness; she bore Ishmael and, by tradition, became an ancestral mother of several Arab peoples (Genesis 16). After conceiving, she fled into the wilderness from Sarah's harsh treatment, and the angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water, promising that her descendants would be too numerous to count and instructing her to return and submit to Sarah.

From this encounter, Hagar named the LORD who spoke to her "Thou God seest me," making her the first person in Scripture recorded as giving God a name (Genesis 16:13). Years later, after Isaac was born, Sarah saw Ishmael mocking him and demanded that Abraham send Hagar and her son away; in the wilderness, with her child near death, God heard her again, opened her eyes to see a well of water, and promised to make Ishmael into a great nation (Genesis 21:9-21).

Hagar's story shows that even a socially marginalized, mistreated foreign servant falls within the reach of God's care — her experience stands as an important biblical witness that God "sees" and attends to the lowly and afflicted.
